name: Mau’s Hōkūleʻa navigation
summary: Micronesian navigator Mau Piailug guided Hōkūleʻa from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti in 1976 without instruments, showing that traditional wayfinding could make such a long voyage.
description: Mau Piailug guided Hōkūleʻa to Tahiti using noninstrument wayfinding.
tier_reason: The scoped record is a particular configuration, local witness, trial or material application. Dependence across fields or generations on THIS referent is not established; do not inherit the importance of its broader missing family.
why: No Hawaiian still held traditional navigation, so the voyaging project recruited Mau from Satawal, where non-instrument navigation was still practised, to test deliberate ancient voyaging.

places.note: Satawal knowledge tradition; Voyage from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti

date.basis: Kyselka’s 1980 account and PVS history date Mau’s guiding voyage to 1976.

events.statement: Mau Piailug guided Hōkūleʻa to Tahiti using noninstrument wayfinding.
events.place_note: Satawal knowledge tradition; Voyage from Hawaiʻi to Tahiti
events.caveats: 1976 dates this voyage, not the origin of Carolinian knowledge. No sweeping claim that all equipment aboard was nonmodern.
